sanskrit: evaṃ vidvān adīnātmā vyasanastho jijīviṣuḥ sarvopāyair upāyajño dīnam ātmānam uddharet
english: Thus the wise man, undaunted in spirit, fallen into calamity yet eager to live, knowing the means, should by every means lift his stricken self out of distress.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya jīvitavyaṃ sadā bhavet jīvan puṇyam avāpnoti naro bhadrāṇi paśyati
english: Holding fast to this resolve, one should ever strive to stay alive; for the man who lives wins merit and beholds good fortune.

sanskrit: tasmāt kaunteya viduṣā dharmādharmaviniścaye buddhim āsthāya loke 'smin vartitavyaṃ yatātmanā
english: Therefore, O son of Kuntī, the wise man, self-controlled, taking his stand upon discernment in distinguishing right from wrong, should conduct himself in this world.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad idaṃ ghoram uddiṣṭam aśraddheyam ivānṛtam asti svid dasyumaryādā yām ahaṃ parivarjaye
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This dreadful teaching that has been set forth seems hardly credible, well-nigh false. Is there indeed any limit of robber-conduct that I might avoid?

sanskrit: saṃmuhyāmi viṣīdāmi dharmo me śithilīkṛtaḥ udyamaṃ nādhigacchāmi kutaś cit paricintayan
english: I am bewildered, I despair; my hold on dharma has been loosened. Ponder as I may, I can find no resolve to act.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca naitac chuddhāgamād eva tava dharmānuśāsanam prajñāsamavatāro 'yaṃ kavibhiḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ madhu
english: Bhīṣma said: This instruction in dharma that I give you does not come from scripture alone; it is a descent of insight, the honey gathered by the wise.

sanskrit: bahvyaḥ pratividhātavyāḥ prajñā rājñā tatas tataḥ naikaśākhena dharmeṇa yātraiṣā saṃpravartate
english: Many kinds of wisdom must a king bring to bear from this side and that; this course of life cannot be carried on by a dharma of a single branch.

sanskrit: buddhisaṃjananaṃ rājñāṃ dharmam ācaratāṃ sadā jayo bhavati kauravya tadā tad viddhi me vacaḥ
english: Wisdom is begotten in kings who ever practice dharma, and then, O Kaurava, victory is theirs: know this as my word.

sanskrit: buddhiśreṣṭhā hi rājāno jayanti vijayaiṣiṇaḥ dharmaḥ pratividhātavyo buddhyā rājñā tatas tataḥ
english: For kings supreme in wisdom, longing for conquest, are the ones who triumph; dharma must be applied by the king with judgment, this way and that.

sanskrit: naikaśākhena dharmeṇa rājñāṃ dharmo vidhīyate durbalasya kutaḥ prajñā purastād anudāhṛtā
english: The dharma of kings is not ordained by a dharma of a single branch; whence should the weak have wisdom, as was set forth before?

sanskrit: advaidhajñaḥ pathi dvaidhe saṃśayaṃ prāptum arhati buddhidvaidhaṃ veditavyaṃ purastād eva bhārata
english: He who knows no doubleness, when the path forks into two, is bound to fall into doubt; the doubleness of judgment must be understood beforehand, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pārśvataḥkaraṇaṃ prajñā viṣūcī tv āpagā iva janas tūccāritaṃ dharmaṃ vijānāty anyathānyathā
english: Wisdom runs to one side and the other, branching like a river; and people understand the dharma that is uttered each in his own differing way.

sanskrit: samyag vijñāninaḥ ke cin mithyāvijñānino 'pare tad vai yathātathaṃ buddhvā jñānam ādadate satām
english: Some have right understanding, others a false one; but the good, having grasped a thing just as it truly is, take up that knowledge.

sanskrit: parimuṣṇanti śāstrāṇi dharmasya paripanthinaḥ vaiṣamyam arthavidyānāṃ nairarthyāt khyāpayanti te
english: The enemies of dharma plunder the scriptures, and out of their emptiness proclaim a discord in the sciences of meaning.

sanskrit: ājijīviṣavo vidyāṃ yaśaskāmāḥ samantataḥ te sarve narapāpiṣṭhā dharmasya paripanthinaḥ
english: Seeking to make a living by learning, hungry for fame on every side—all such are the vilest of men, the enemies of dharma.

sanskrit: apakvamatayo mandā na jānanti yathātatham sadā hy aśāstrakuśalāḥ sarvatrāpariniṣṭhitāḥ
english: Of unripe mind and dull, they do not know things as they truly are; ever unskilled in the scriptures, they are nowhere firmly grounded.

sanskrit: parimuṣṇanti śāstrāṇi śāstradoṣānudarśinaḥ vijñānam atha vidyānāṃ na samyag iti vartate
english: Those who look only for faults in the scriptures plunder them; and so the understanding of the sciences proceeds astray, not aright.

sanskrit: nindayā paravidyānāṃ svāṃ vidyāṃ khyāpayanti ye vāgastrā vākchurīmattvā dugdhavidyāphalā iva tān vidyāvaṇijo viddhi rākṣasān iva bhārata
english: Those who by belittling the learning of others advertise their own—armed with speech, drunk on the daggers of their words, as though they had milked dry the fruit of learning—know them, O Bhārata, for hucksters of knowledge, like very rākṣasas.

sanskrit: vyājena kṛtsno vidito dharmas te parihāsyate na dharmavacanaṃ vācā na buddhyā ceti naḥ śrutam
english: If the whole of dharma is known to you through pretext, it will desert you; for we have heard that the declaring of dharma is not by mere speech, nor by mere cleverness.

sanskrit: iti bārhaspataṃ jñānaṃ provāca maghavā svayam na tv eva vacanaṃ kiṃ cid animittād ihocyate
english: So Maghavat himself declared the teaching of Bṛhaspati; and yet no word here is uttered without a ground.

sanskrit: svavinītena śāstreṇa vyavasyanti tathāpare lokayātrām ihaike tu dharmam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: By the discipline they have learned for themselves some others resolve their course; but the wise here call the conduct of worldly life itself dharma.

sanskrit: samuddiṣṭaṃ satāṃ dharmaṃ svayam ūhen na paṇḍitaḥ amarṣāc chāstrasaṃmohād avijñānāc ca bhārata
english: The dharma laid down by the good a learned man should not reason away on his own out of impatience, from confusion over the scriptures, or from ignorance, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śāstraṃ prājñasya vadataḥ samūhe yāty adarśanam āgatāgamayā buddhyā vacanena praśasyate
english: When a wise man speaks in an assembly, scripture passes out of sight; he is approved for his speech, by a judgment grounded in tradition received.

sanskrit: ajñānāj jñānahetutvād vacanaṃ sādhu manyate anapāhatam evedaṃ nedaṃ śāstram apārthakam
english: Out of ignorance, because his word is a source of knowledge, men deem it sound; this is not to be cast aside, this scripture is not without purpose.

sanskrit: daiteyān uśanāḥ prāha saṃśayacchedane purā jñānam avyapadeśyaṃ hi yathā nāsti tathaiva tat
english: Uśanas of old said to the Daityas, when resolving their doubts: just as there is no knowledge that cannot be made plain, so indeed it is.

sanskrit: tena tvaṃ chinnamūlena kaṃ toṣayitum arhasi atathyavihitaṃ yo vā nedaṃ vākyam upāśnuyāt
english: Whom can you satisfy with that whose root is cut? And who would heed this speech laid down upon what is untrue?

sanskrit: ugrāyaiva hi sṛṣṭo 'si karmaṇe na tv avekṣase aṅgemām anvavekṣasva rājanītiṃ bubhūṣitum yayā pramucyate tv anyo yadarthaṃ ca pramodate
english: For you were created for fierce action, yet you will not look to it. Come, consider this statecraft, if you wish to thrive—the polity by which one man is set free and for whose sake another rejoices.

sanskrit: ajo 'śvaḥ kṣatram ity etat sadṛśaṃ brahmaṇā kṛtam tasmān natīkṣṇabhūtānāṃ yātrā kā cit prasidhyati
english: The goat, the horse, the warrior—these were made alike by Brahmā; hence for those whose nature is not fierce no course of life can succeed.

sanskrit: yas tv avadhyavadhe doṣaḥ sa vadhyasyāvadhe smṛtaḥ eṣaiva khalu maryādā yām ayaṃ parivarjayet
english: The fault that lies in slaying one who ought not to be slain is held to lie equally in not slaying one who ought to be slain; this very thing is the limit a king must not transgress.

sanskrit: tasmāt tīkṣṇaḥ prajā rājā svadharme sthāpayed uta anyonyaṃ bhakṣayanto hi pracareyur vṛkā iva
english: Therefore let the king, stern, establish his subjects each in their own duty; for otherwise they would range about devouring one another like wolves.

sanskrit: yasya dasyugaṇā rāṣṭre dhvāṅkṣā matsyāñ jalād iva viharanti parasvāni sa vai kṣatriyapāṃsanaḥ
english: That king in whose realm bands of robbers make away with others' goods—as crows snatch fish from the water—is verily a disgrace to the warrior caste.

sanskrit: kulīnān sacivān kṛtvā vedavidyāsamanvitān praśādhi pṛthivīṃ rājan prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
english: Making well-born men your counsellors, men endowed with knowledge of the Veda, rule the earth, O king, protecting your subjects by dharma.

sanskrit: vihīnajam akarmāṇaṃ yaḥ pragṛhṇāti bhūmipaḥ ubhayasyāviśeṣajñas tad vai kṣatraṃ napuṃsakam
english: The lord of earth who takes up a man of low birth and no fit deeds, knowing no difference between the two, makes of his warrior-rule a thing unmanned.

sanskrit: naivograṃ naiva cānugraṃ dharmeṇeha praśasyate ubhayaṃ na vyatikrāmed ugro bhūtvā mṛdur bhava
english: Neither the wholly fierce nor the wholly gentle is here commended by dharma; transgress neither extreme—having been fierce, become mild.

sanskrit: kaṣṭaḥ kṣatriyadharmo 'yaṃ sauhṛdaṃ tvayi yat sthitam ugre karmaṇi sṛṣṭo 'si tasmād rājyaṃ praśādhi vai
english: Hard is this duty of the warrior, in whom such tenderness abides; you were created for fierce action—therefore rule the kingdom.

sanskrit: aśiṣṭanigraho nityaṃ śiṣṭasya paripālanam iti śakro 'bravīd dhīmān āpatsu bharatarṣabha
english: The constant restraint of the unruly, the guarding of the well-disciplined—thus spoke the wise Śakra concerning times of distress, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca asti svid dasyumaryādā yām anyo nātilaṅghayet pṛcchāmi tvāṃ satāṃ śreṣṭha tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Is there indeed a limit even of robbers that another should not overstep? I ask you, O best of the good—tell me this, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca brāhmaṇān eva seveta vidyāvṛddhāṃs tapasvinaḥ śrutacāritravṛttāḍhyān pavitraṃ hy etad uttamam
english: Bhīṣma said: One should serve the brāhmaṇas, men grown great in learning, ascetics, rich in sacred lore, good character, and conduct; for this is the highest purification.

sanskrit: yā devatāsu vṛttis te sāstu vipreṣu sarvadā kruddhair hi vipraiḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni bahudhā nṛpa
english: The conduct you keep toward the gods—let that be yours toward the brāhmaṇas always; for by brāhmaṇas in their wrath deeds of many kinds have been wrought, O king.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prītyā yaśo mukhyam aprītyā tu viparyayaḥ prītyā hy amṛtavad viprāḥ kruddhāś caiva yathā viṣam
english: From their favor comes foremost glory, from their displeasure the reverse; for when pleased the brāhmaṇas are like nectar, and when enraged like poison.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña sarvaśāstraviśārada śaraṇaṃ pālayānasya yo dharmas taṃ vadasva me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Grandfather, great in wisdom, versed in all the scriptures, tell me the dharma of one who protects a suppliant who has sought his shelter.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mahān dharmo mahārāja śaraṇāgatapālane arhaḥ praṣṭuṃ bhavāṃś caiva praśnaṃ bharatasattama
english: Bhīṣma said: Great is the dharma, O great king, in the protection of one who has come for refuge; and you indeed are worthy to ask this question, best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: nṛgaprabhṛtayo rājan rājānaḥ śaraṇāgatān paripālya mahārāja saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ
english: Kings beginning with Nṛga, O king, having protected those who came to them for refuge, attained, O great monarch, the highest perfection.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi kapotena śatruḥ śaraṇam āgataḥ pūjitaś ca yathānyāyaṃ svaiś ca māṃsair nimantritaḥ
english: For it is told how, by a dove, an enemy who had come for refuge was honored as was right and entertained with the bird's own flesh.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ kapotena purā śatruḥ śaraṇam āgataḥ svamāṃsair bhojitaḥ kāṃ ca gatiṃ lebhe sa bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was it that long ago an enemy came for refuge to a dove and was fed with the bird's own flesh, and what destiny did that dove attain, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu rājan kathāṃ divyāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm nṛpater mucukundasya kathitāṃ bhārgaveṇa ha
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, O king, a divine tale, destroyer of all sins, told to King Mucukunda by Bhārgava of old.

sanskrit: imam arthaṃ purā pārtha mucukundo narādhipaḥ bhārgavaṃ paripapraccha praṇato bharatarṣabha
english: This very matter, O Pārtha, the king Mucukunda asked of Bhārgava in days gone by, bowing low, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tasmai śuśrūṣamāṇāya bhārgavo 'kathayat kathām iyaṃ yathā kapotena siddhiḥ prāptā narādhipa
english: To him as he sat attentive, Bhārgava told the tale of how perfection was won by the dove, O lord of men.

sanskrit: dharmaniścayasaṃyuktāṃ kāmārthasahitāṃ kathām śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājan gadato me mahābhuja
english: A tale joined with the settled truths of dharma and bound up with desire and gain—hear it attentively, O king, mighty-armed, as I tell it.

sanskrit: kaś cit kṣudrasamācāraḥ pṛthivyāṃ kālasaṃmataḥ cacāra pṛthivīṃ pāpo ghoraḥ śakunilubdhakaḥ
english: A certain man of base conduct, reckoned as cruel as Death itself, ranged over the earth, sinful and dreadful, a fowler of birds.

sanskrit: kākola iva kṛṣṇāṅgo rūkṣaḥ pāpasamāhitaḥ yavamadhyaḥ kṛśagrīvo hrasvapādo mahāhanuḥ
english: Black-limbed as a raven, harsh, bent wholly upon evil, narrow at the waist, thin-necked, short-legged, and great of jaw.

sanskrit: naiva tasya suhṛt kaś cin na saṃbandhī na bāndhavaḥ sa hi taiḥ saṃparityaktas tena ghoreṇa karmaṇā
english: He had no friend at all, no kinsman, no relation; for by all of these he had been cast off because of that dreadful trade of his.

sanskrit: sa vai kṣārakam ādāya dvijān hatvā vane sadā cakāra vikrayaṃ teṣāṃ pataṃgānāṃ narādhipa
english: Taking up his cage, he would forever kill the birds in the forest and make a trade of those winged creatures, O lord of men.

sanskrit: evaṃ tu vartamānasya tasya vṛttiṃ durātmanaḥ agamat sumahān kālo na cādharmam abudhyata
english: While that evil-souled man lived thus by his livelihood, a very long time passed, and yet he did not perceive his own unrighteousness.

sanskrit: tasya bhāryāsahāyasya ramamāṇasya śāśvatam daivayogavimūḍhasya nānyā vṛttir arocata
english: To him, with his wife for sole companion, taking his constant pleasure, bewildered by the working of fate, no other way of life seemed good.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit tasyātha vanasthasya samudgataḥ pātayann iva vṛkṣāṃs tān sumahān vātasaṃbhramaḥ
english: Then once, as he stood in the forest, there arose a great tumult of wind, as though casting down the very trees.

sanskrit: meghasaṃkulam ākāśaṃ vidyunmaṇḍalamaṇḍitam saṃchannaṃ sumuhūrtena nausthāneneva sāgaraḥ
english: The sky grew thick with clouds, adorned with circling lightnings, and in a moment was wholly covered, like a harbor crowded with the ships of the sea.

sanskrit: vāridhārāsamūhaiś ca saṃprahṛṣṭaḥ śatakratuḥ kṣaṇena pūrayām āsa salilena vasuṃdharām
english: And the god of a hundred sacrifices, rejoicing, with masses of streaming rain filled the earth with water in an instant.

sanskrit: tato dhārākule loke saṃbhraman naṣṭacetanaḥ śītārtas tad vanaṃ sarvam ākulenāntarātmanā
english: Then, while the world was awhirl with the downpour, he wandered, his wits gone, tormented by the cold, all through that forest, his inmost soul in turmoil.

sanskrit: naiva nimnaṃ sthalaṃ vāpi so 'vindata vihaṃgahā pūrito hi jalaughena mārgas tasya vanasya vai
english: That slayer of birds could find neither low ground nor high; for the path through that forest was filled with the flood of waters.

sanskrit: pakṣiṇo vātavegena hatā līnās tadābhavan mṛgāḥ siṃhā varāhāś ca sthalāny āśritya tasthire
english: The birds, struck down by the force of the wind, lay then huddled close; the deer, the lions, and the boars stood crowded upon the high ground.

sanskrit: mahatā vātavarṣeṇa trāsitās te vanaukasaḥ bhayārtāś ca kṣudhārtāś ca babhramuḥ sahitā vane
english: Terrified by the mighty wind and rain, those dwellers of the forest, distressed by fear and tormented by hunger, wandered together through the wood.

sanskrit: sa tu śītahatair gātrair jagāmaiva na tasthivān so 'paśyad vanaṣaṇḍeṣu meghanīlaṃ vanaspatim
english: But he, his limbs smitten by the cold, kept moving and did not halt; and amid the thickets of the wood he spied a great tree dark as a raincloud.

sanskrit: tārāḍhyaṃ kumudākāram ākāśaṃ nirmalaṃ ca ha meghair muktaṃ nabho dṛṣṭvā lubdhakaḥ śītavihvalaḥ
english: Seeing the heaven grown rich with stars, fair as the white lily, clear and freed of clouds, the fowler, undone by the cold,

sanskrit: diśo 'valokayām āsa velāṃ caiva durātmavān dūre grāmaniveśaś ca tasmād deśād iti prabho kṛtabuddhir vane tasmin vastuṃ tāṃ rajanīṃ tadā
english: that evil-souled man looked about him at the quarters of the sky and at the hour; and since the nearest village lay far from that spot, O lord, he made up his mind to dwell that night there in the forest.

sanskrit: so 'ñjaliṃ prayataḥ kṛtvā vākyam āha vanaspatim śaraṇaṃ yāmi yāny asmin daivatānīha bhārata
english: Reverently folding his hands, he spoke to the tree: I go for refuge to whatever divinities dwell here in this place, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa śilāyāṃ śiraḥ kṛtvā parṇāny āstīrya bhūtale duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭas tataḥ suṣvāpa pakṣihā
english: Laying his head upon a stone and strewing leaves over the ground, that slayer of birds, overcome with great misery, then fell asleep.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atha vṛkṣasya śākhāyāṃ vihaṃgaḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ dīrghakāloṣito rājaṃs tatra citratanūruhaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Now upon a branch of that tree, O king, a bird with his dear mate had long dwelt there, his plumage bright and varied.

sanskrit: tasya kālyaṃ gatā bhāryā carituṃ nābhyavartata prāptāṃ ca rajanīṃ dṛṣṭvā sa pakṣī paryatapyata
english: His mate had gone forth at dawn to forage and had not returned; and seeing that night had come on, the bird grew sore distressed.

sanskrit: vātavarṣaṃ mahac cāsīn na cāgacchati me priyā kiṃ nu tat kāraṇaṃ yena sādyāpi na nivartate
english: Great was the wind and rain, and my beloved does not come. What can be the cause that even now she has not returned?

sanskrit: api svasti bhavet tasyāḥ priyāyā mama kānane tayā virahitaṃ hīdaṃ śūnyam adya gṛhaṃ mama
english: May it be well with my beloved out there in the forest! For without her this home of mine is empty today.

sanskrit: yadi sā raktanetrāntā citrāṅgī madhurasvarā adya nābhyeti me kāntā na kāryaṃ jīvitena me
english: If she of the red-cornered eyes, of dappled body and sweet voice, my darling, does not come to me today, then I have no use for life.

sanskrit: patidharmaratā sādhvī prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī sā hi śrāntaṃ kṣudhārtaṃ ca jānīte māṃ tapasvinī
english: Devoted to the duty of a wife, virtuous, dearer to me than my own breath—that gentle creature knows when I am weary and tormented by hunger.

sanskrit: anuraktā hitā caiva snigdhā caiva pativratā yasya vai tādṛśī bhāryā dhanyaḥ sa manujo bhuvi
english: Loving and devoted to his good, tender and faithful to her lord—the man on earth who has such a wife is blessed indeed.

sanskrit: bhāryā hi paramo nāthaḥ puruṣasyeha paṭhyate asahāyasya loke 'smiṃl lokayātrāsahāyinī
english: A wife is declared to be a man's highest protector here, the companion in life's journey for one who in this world is otherwise without help.

sanskrit: tathā rogābhibhūtasya nityaṃ kṛcchragatasya ca nāsti bhāryāsamaṃ kiṃ cin narasyārtasya bheṣajam
english: So too for a man overwhelmed by sickness and ever sunk in hardship, there is no medicine for one in distress like a wife.

sanskrit: nāsti bhāryāsamo bandhur nāsti bhāryāsamā gatiḥ nāsti bhāryāsamo loke sahāyo dharmasādhanaḥ
english: There is no kinsman like a wife, no refuge like a wife; in all the world there is no helper like a wife for the accomplishing of dharma.

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapatas tasya dvijasyārtasya tatra vai gṛhītā śakunaghnena bhāryā śuśrāva bhāratīm
english: As the bird thus lamented there in his grief, his mate, who had been seized by the slayer of birds, heard his speech.

sanskrit: na sā strīty abhibhāṣā syād yasyā bhartā na tuṣyati agnisākṣikam apy etad bhartā hi śaraṇaṃ striyaḥ
english: She whose husband is not content with her should not be called a woman at all; for, with the fire itself as witness, the husband is the refuge of a wife.

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya duḥkhārtā bhartāraṃ duḥkhitaṃ tadā kapotī lubdhakenātha yattā vacanam abravīt
english: Reflecting thus, stricken with grief, the hen-dove then, held captive by the fowler, addressed her sorrowing husband with these well-weighed words.
